> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **28** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8c7021dfb43bd35863ec65311d472f3eff8a8204` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d0ea69991f4c6656136a0c51dbb0c0e9f9edf093` — the merge of head `b23188c1485cb54d6de2658d7e3a5818b58b4fc0` into base `8c7021dfb43bd35863ec65311d472f3eff8a8204`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d0ea69991f4c6656136a0c51dbb0c0e9f9edf093 && git checkout d0ea69991f4c6656136a0c51dbb0c0e9f9edf093
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8c7021dfb43bd35863ec65311d472f3eff8a8204 b23188c1485cb54d6de2658d7e3a5818b58b4fc0 && git checkout -B drift-repro 8c7021dfb43bd35863ec65311d472f3eff8a8204 && git merge --no-ff b23188c1485cb54d6de2658d7e3a5818b58b4fc0

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8c7021dfb43bd35863ec65311d472f3eff8a8204
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 8c7021dfb43bd35863ec65311d472f3eff8a8204` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b23188c1485cb54d6de2658d7e3a5818b58b4fc0`
Local-runs: none
Scope: docs/adr/0104-field-runtime-value-shape-contract.md, packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/actions.ts + packages/spec/src/ui/action-params.zod.ts (`validateActionParams`, `ACTION_PARAM_BUILTIN_KEYS`), packages/runtime/src/error-envelope.ts (`buildApiError`, `apiErrorResponse`, `splitSemanticCode`), packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts (`deps.error`, the 5xx `looksLikeInternalErrorLeak` arm, `errorFromThrown`), packages/types/src/thrown-http-error.ts (`resolveThrownHttpError`), packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts (`run_action` catch, `errorResultFromThrown`, `errorResultWithCode`), packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/sys-approval-request.object.ts (`approval_approve` / `approval_reject` declarations), packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts (the decide path's `outputs` judgment against `decisionOutputs`), ui/packages/app-shell/src/hooks/useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx (the console's `outputs.` fold), docs/adr/0066-unified-authorization-model.md (D4, amended 2026-10-29), scripts/check-route-envelope.mjs (the `actions.ts` ledger row). The remainder of the diff (`.changeset/*`, the two test files) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

Inputs read: card #27738 body and every comment (cross-seat note 6510971608, retriage 6513014687, triage first touch 6513120708, claim 6513796817, dev report 6514467517); PR #27915 body, file list and the net diff against `main` (`git diff origin/main...b23188c1`, merge base `b13a1ed3`); the cited code on `origin/main` and at the head; the head's check-runs read at 2026-10-30T03:56Z. The tree was judged, not the PR body's account of it.

**Check-runs on the head at 2026-10-30T03:56Z:** every completed non-skipped run is `success` (Lint · ESLint, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · CI/release/engine gates, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, the three scoped lints, Type Check · workspace / source gates / consumer gates / debt ledger, Check Changeset, Check PR Size, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check Documentation Links, Dogfood Regression Gate, Test UI, Live E2E UI, Test Core 1/8, 6/8, 7/8). Still `in_progress`: Build Core, Test Core 2/8, 3/8, 4/8, 5/8, 8/8. Pending is pending: this record's PASS is on the design and the derived judgments; the landing still waits on green and, this being Tier H (`docs/adr/**`), on a `GOVERNED_APPROVERS` review.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, read in the tree:

1. **ADR-0104 D2 accept set widens by one undeclared family, scoped by a predicate — right.** `enforceActionParams` (action-execution.ts L2473) now hands `validateActionParams` the bag through `paramBagUnderContract`, which drops an entry only when (a) `foldsApiDecisionOutputs(action)` holds — `type === 'api'`, `!isDeclarativeUpdateAction`, no string `bodyShape.wrap` — and (b) `isApiDecisionOutputParam(key)` holds — the `outputs.` prefix with a non-empty remainder — and (c) the key is not among the resolved declared names. Everything else reaches the unchanged spec validator, so the `unknown_field` refusal, the required/shape judgments and `OS_ALLOW_LAX_ACTION_PARAMS` are byte-identical for every other key. `packages/spec` is untouched (confirmed: no `packages/spec` path in the file list; `ACTION_PARAM_BUILTIN_KEYS` unchanged), matching the claim's hard constraint.
2. **Both doors share the one gate — right.** The REST door calls `enforceActionParams` at domains/actions.ts L731 with `reqBody.params`; the MCP bridge calls it at action-execution.ts L3357 (`invokeBusinessAction`). One edit widens both, which is what the ADR amendment states.
3. **The fold and the admission share one predicate — right.** `buildApiActionRequest`'s existing `outputs.` fold (L1312) now asks `isApiDecisionOutputParam`; the admission asks the same function. The fold's scope (flat body only; under `bodyShape.wrap` the params are nested and the loop over `Object.keys(body)` never sees them) is exactly what `foldsApiDecisionOutputs` encodes, so the admission reaches as far as the fold and no further. The console's own fold (`useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx` L460: `k.startsWith('outputs.') && k.length > 'outputs.'.length`) is the same rule, so the ADR's "the console folds the same family by the same rule" is true in the tree.
4. **Reading on scope breadth:** the admission is for every flat-body `type: 'api'` action, not only approvals routes. The door cannot know a target's semantics, and an admitted `outputs.KEY` is folded and sent to a target the caller can already call directly with any body under the same credentials, so no capability is added; the target judges (`approval-service.ts` L4456–4506: undeclared keys refused with `VALIDATION_FAILED`, `required` enforced). The ADR amendment states this scope in plain words. Right, and correctly recorded.
5. **REST refusal envelope: the target's `error` members are relayed, not rebuilt — right.** `apiActionRefusalMembers` admits only `{ success: false, error: { code: non-empty string } }` bodies and returns every `error` member except `code`, `message`, `httpStatus`. `actions.ts` then builds through `apiErrorResponse({ message, httpStatus: answer.status, code, extra: members })`. In `buildApiError` the `extra` spread sits after `code`/`message`/`httpStatus`, and those three are excluded from `members`, so a target cannot override the door's code, sentence or status through `extra`; `details` passed as `undefined` means `splitSemanticCode` promotes nothing and the target's `details` ride through `extra` unchanged. The un-enveloped branch (`members === undefined`) is the pre-change `deps.error(message, status, { code })` call, so a better-auth `{ code, message }`, a non-JSON or an empty body answer exactly as before. The forward's own synthetic 502 (non-JSON 2xx) is enveloped with a safe message by `forwardApiAction` itself. One shared helper, no new code minted, `check:route-envelope`'s `handBuilt: 3` for `actions.ts` holds (one response site for both refusal answers) — right.
6. **MCP `run_action`: `details` ride the throw — right, and bounded.** `apiActionForwardRefusal` adds `details` only when present. `run_action`'s catch renders through `errorResultFromThrown`, which reads `.details` off a coded throw and, for `PERMISSION_DENIED` alone, routes to `errorResultWithCode` and withholds them — the #23529 rule stays in force for the forwarded refusal too. `resolveThrownHttpError` does not read `.details` off a throw, so the REST path is unaffected by the extra property (and it never reaches it: the REST api branch returns a response rather than throwing).
7. **Public surface: none.** `isApiDecisionOutputParam`, `foldsApiDecisionOutputs`, `apiActionRefusalMembers` are exported from `action-execution.ts`, which `packages/runtime/src/index.ts` does not re-export and `package.json` exposes no subpath for (`"."` only). Nothing an author writes changes.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/27738-api-action-door-refusal-and-decision-outputs.md`: `@objectstack/runtime: patch`, with `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` line-initial in both the changeset and the PR body — matches the claim's declaration. Under AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3 the level follows the protocol kind alone: `none` takes `patch`, and "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch`". The diff moves no spec key, no authorable value and no package export (①.7), so `patch` is the rule's answer, not a judgment call; the dispatch's "minor if the widening is a published behaviour" is overridden by the written rule, and the dev justified the deviation in the changeset as required. `Check Changeset` is green on the head. The `Clause-②: yes (widening)` arm is the right one: the D2 accept set grows, nothing is refused that was accepted. ✔ Level and lines are right.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev-flagged deviations (report 6514467517), each answered:

- **(a) `patch`, not `minor`.** Answered in ②: correct under AGENTS.md step 3. Not a deviation from the rule, only from the dispatch's conditional wording.
- **(b) MCP `run_action` also carries the target's `details`.** Accepted. The triage ruling named G1 at the REST api branch; the claim's file surface already included `apiActionForwardRefusal` under G1. The two doors run "the identical sequence" by ADR-0066 D4's own text, so a `details` member one door relays and the other drops would be a new asymmetry at the seam the ruling is closing. Bounded by `errorResultFromThrown`'s `PERMISSION_DENIED` withholding (①.6). Pinned (the MCP-details case) and ablated (A2). One asymmetry remains and is noted, not a finding on this PR: REST now relays `userMessage`, while `run_action`'s renderer reads only `code`, `message`, `status` and `details` off a throw (`ThrownRefusalEnvelope` in `packages/mcp`, outside the surface), so `userMessage` does not reach an MCP client. For the seat to file if a consumer wants it.
- **(c) The enveloped REST relay skips `deps.error`'s 5xx message heuristic.** Accepted, with the reading stated. `HttpDispatcher.error` applies `looksLikeInternalErrorLeak` only to `message` and only at `httpStatus >= 500`. Every target boundary a same-origin path can resolve to already applies the same predicate to what it emits (`HttpDispatcher.error`, the Hono adapter's arm at `adapters/hono/src/index.ts` L755 and L1006, the REST registrars and `plugin-hono-server` per their recorded changes), so the body the forward reads is post-discipline; re-running the heuristic at the door would only differ by withholding a message the target's boundary decided to serve — a `refusal: true` declared message, for instance, which the dispatcher's own `#12509` rule exists to let through. A direct caller receives the same text. Consistent with "relay whole"; the un-enveloped branch keeps the heuristic. Judged right.
- **(d) Cross-seat note item 2 (`apiActionResultOf` on a 200 `{ success: false }`) not folded.** Agreed. `apiActionResultOf` unwraps `data` when both `success` and `data` are present and returns the body otherwise; turning a target's 2xx into a non-2xx at the door is a decision about the status the door answers, not about which members a refusal carries, and no producer was measured (the note says so). Draft PR #27793 already reads a relayed 200 rejection inside `data` as a failure on the console side, so the first consumer is not blocked by it. Escalated to the seat to file as its own card (dedupe words in the dev report).

`open_questions`: the dev report lists none. Out-of-scope finding on `scripts/check-route-envelope.mjs` L981 (the ledger note still says "`deps.error` spread" for the non-2xx relay): outside the face and the surface; the count holds and the gate is green; for the seat, not this PR.

**G1 security reading (the relay of `error.details` and `userMessage` whole).** Premise, confirmed in the tree: the target is same-origin and in-process (`resolveInProcessRequest`), the forward carries only the caller's own identity headers (`API_FORWARD_HEADER_ALLOWLIST`: `authorization`, `cookie`, `x-admin-session-token`, `x-tenant-id`, `x-environment-id`, `x-api-key`, plus browser provenance and proxy headers "as the caller sent them"), and adds nothing privileged — only `accept: application/json`, `content-type`, and the loop mark `x-objectstack-action-forward`, which no target reads as trust. So the target authorizes the same principal and answers the same body it would answer to that caller's direct call; the forward reads that body after the target's boundary has applied its own withholding (the dispatcher's `PERMISSION_DENIED` diagnostics withholding at `http-dispatcher.ts` L3132, the 5xx leak rule). Relaying it whole therefore discloses to the caller exactly what the caller could already read by calling the target, and nothing the door previously withheld from a caller who could not otherwise see it: the door's own gates (401 floor, D4, ADR-0126 §8, the subject load) still run before the forward, and a caller those gates refuse never reaches the relay. The MCP door is stricter than REST by one rule (`PERMISSION_DENIED` details withheld), which is REST/MCP parity as it stands today for every other refusal and is unchanged here. Reading: no new disclosure. The one residual is the premise itself — if a future `target` resolver ever reached off-origin or ran with a different principal, the relay would carry a third party's body; `isSameOriginApiTarget` and the allow-list are the pins, both outside this diff and both unchanged.

### ④ Design judgment

**`docs/adr/0104-field-runtime-value-shape-contract.md`** — judged against its first consumer (#27611 / draft PR #27793, which sends `outputs.KEY` params for a request's `decision_outputs` through the door) and its execution plan (this PR). The status-line entry and the D2 item-1 note state who admits (the gate, both doors), what (the `outputs.KEY` family, prefix plus non-empty key), for which actions (`type: 'api'`, not a declarative update, no `bodyShape.wrap`), who judges the values (the target, against the request's `decisionOutputs`, ADR-0066 D4), and what does not change (declared params judged as declared; every other undeclared key refused; the family refused where nothing folds it; the lax switch; the spec validator and its built-ins). Each sentence is true in the tree (①.1–①.4) and each cited symbol exists at the cited path (`buildApiActionRequest`, `enforceActionParams`, `foldsApiDecisionOutputs`, `isApiDecisionOutputParam`, `validateActionParams` in `action-params.zod.ts`). The consumer's need is met exactly: `approval_approve` / `approval_reject` declare `params: [comment, attachments]`, are `type: 'api'` with a flat body, so the console's `outputs.KEY` params pass the gate and are folded into `outputs` for `/approvals/requests/{id}/approve|reject`, whose decide path enforces declared keys and `required`. Tried to break it: a declared dotted `outputs.reason` param stays judged (declared names are excluded from the drop); `outputs.` bare and `output.reason` stay refused; a declarative update with `type: 'api'` is excluded by `operation` first, matching the #15079 ordering; a wrapped body is excluded because the fold cannot reach it. The amendment adds no rule beyond what the code does and is dated and cross-referenced the way the 2026-10-19 and 2026-10-26 entries are. No finding.

**`packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts`** — `paramBagUnderContract` is a pure projection applied only to the bag the spec validator sees; the bag the handler and `buildApiActionRequest` receive is unchanged, so the fold still sees every `outputs.KEY` (including a blank one it omits). `apiActionRefusalMembers` is strict on the envelope shape (object, `success === false`, `error` object with a non-empty string `code`) and returns `{}` rather than `undefined` for an envelope that carries nothing beside the three fixed members; that `{}` is truthy, so such a refusal takes the `apiErrorResponse` branch — the output is identical to the `deps.error` branch except for the 5xx heuristic, which ③(c) judges, so it is a consistent reading of "enveloped ⇒ relayed", not a defect. `apiActionForwardRefusal` stamps `details` conditionally, so a throw without them is byte-identical to before. `apiBodyWrap` is the one reader of `bodyShape.wrap`, extracted from the fold without changing its predicate. No finding.

**`packages/runtime/src/domains/actions.ts`** — the api branch's refusal answer is one `response:` site spreading either envelope helper plus the relayed rotation headers; both helpers are the declared envelope builders, so the ADR-0112 shape is kept by construction and `error-envelope.conformance` / `check:route-envelope` are green on the head. `code` precedence: `apiActionForwardRefusal`'s code (envelope `error.code`, else top-level `code`, else status-derived) is passed explicitly and wins. No finding.

**Findings:** no must-fix. No should-fix on the face files. Two notes for the seat, neither a defect in this PR: the MCP `userMessage` asymmetry (③b) and the `check-route-envelope.mjs` ledger wording (③). Cross-seat note item 2 is escalated for a card (③d).

## 维护者速读

## 席位核对

Head-sha: `b23188c1485cb54d6de2658d7e3a5818b58b4fc0`

- **Shape:** G1 — the api branch relays the target's refusal members unchanged (`apiActionRefusalMembers` keeps `details` and `userMessage`, excludes `code` / `message` / `httpStatus` so they cannot override the door's own), through one response site (`check:route-envelope` stays at `handBuilt: 3`); MCP `run_action` carries `details` too, bounded by `errorResultFromThrown`'s `PERMISSION_DENIED` withholding. G2 — `outputs.KEY` is admitted only for `type: 'api'` actions whose request `buildApiActionRequest` folds, by one predicate shared by the fold and the admission, at the one gate both doors call; `packages/spec` untouched. ADR-0104 carries a dated amendment naming the widened set. Changeset `@objectstack/runtime` patch (`Metadata-protocol: none` ⇒ patch per AGENTS.md step 3), `Clause-②: yes (widening)`. `check-governed-merges --pr 27915`: GOVERNED (`docs/adr/**`), Tier H, 439 changed lines.
- **Premise measured:** on a booted showcase through the public door: G1a recalc 400 `FLOW_FAILED` — before no `details`, after byte-identical to the direct call; G1b entitlement 403 — before no `details`, after identical; G2 `approval_approve` with `outputs.next_reviewers` — before 400 `Unknown action param`, after 200 and the request approved. Red first 8 failed / 38 passed, after 46/46 (dev report 6514467517 on #27738).
- **Gate check-runs on the head:** 49 runs, 36 success, 13 skipped, 0 failure/pending; `mergeable_state` clean.
